versions.rationale: One patch for the focused content correction; no pre-existing unpublished bump.

findingsCorrected.problem: The ownership recipe transferred a received delivery/permit after successful handler submission without defining the actual rejection-policy contract. A normal execute return can silently drop a new delivery or evict an older queued delivery; cleanup never runs.
findingsCorrected.evidence: Java SE 25 policy contracts and deterministic real ThreadPoolExecutor saturation/shutdown controls.
findingsCorrected.change: Require observable dispatch ownership; inspect actual factory/configuration, queue, rejection handler and wrappers. Preserve visible rejection plus caller recovery or explicit settlement of every discarded item. Do not run the handler while holding the gate used to close intake.
findingsCorrected.consequence: Prevents interpreting a bounded executor or successful method return as proof that every broker delivery has a local owner.

findingsCorrected.problem: Generic submission rejection injection did not ensure the actual policy was triggered or account for eviction of a previously queued delivery.
findingsCorrected.change: Include silent-discard outcomes at intake; force actual saturation and post-shutdown submission with the configured policy and reconcile every received ID and permit.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A test must expose the specific delivery lost at dispatch, including an older item, rather than only check the newest submission or executor termination.

capabilitiesPreserved: Conditional decision to use task queues, per-key lanes, independent subscription queues or a replayable log; no forced migration.
Broker-specific SQS/RabbitMQ/JMS acknowledgement, redelivery and stale receipt distinctions; ack placement stays with delivery-semantics.
Measured receive-to-ack exposure, censored tails, prefetch waves, finite renewal, last grant and uncertain extension accounting.
Repeat-safe effects and resource guards without treating a lease, fence or conditional failure as deduplication proof.
Finite local and uncertain-recovery ownership budgets, partial batch outcomes, cleanup and shutdown reconciliation.
Conditional autoscaling with age/depth/rates/capacity assumptions, priority service contracts and tenant/security bounds.
Adequate existing designs may remain unchanged; scoped explanations need not implement a worker or a crash campaign.

compatibility.skillBaseline: Preserve each consuming project's deployed Java, broker and client/framework baseline. No baseline changed.
compatibility.changedShippedCode: Pseudocode and guidance only; existing conceptual ScheduledExecutorService snippet unchanged.
compatibility.dependencies: None added or upgraded; standard JDK only.
compatibility.limitation: Java 17 compiler compatibility checked; no Java 17 runtime execution claimed.
